title: Vendor assurance 1:1 prep memo — Sloane
body:
Purpose / goals:
- Prep for 1:1 with Vendor Assurance lead (internal) before the vendor kick-off call next week.
- Make sure we have a clear ask list for SOC2/ISO evidence, bridge letters, and right-to-audit scope.
- Align on who will own evidence collection and how to store artifacts for the external auditor.

Top-line agenda for the 1:1 (30m):
1) Quick status (3m): which vendors are critical this quarter, any red flags.
2) Evidence matrix review (10m): what we need vs what vendor can provide.
3) Logistics (8m): secure transfer, TTL, naming convention, access roles.
4) Negotiation levers (5m): right-to-audit, bridge letters, remediation timelines.
5) Action items & owners (4m).

Prep checklist (bring to meeting):
- Current vendor inventory filtered to Tier 1 & Tier 2 (contract link + service description).
- Most recent SOC2 / ISO attestation (if vendor provided previously).
- Contract snippets that mention security obligations (RTAs, breach notif SLA).
- Proposed evidence bucket name and IAM role for auditors.
- Proposed artifact naming convention: vendorname_controlID_YYYYMMDD.pdf

Evidence ask matrix (working draft):
- SOC2 Type II (last 12 months) OR SOC2 bridge letter if report is older than 12 months.
- Encryption at rest: KMS policy excerpt, key rotation schedule, and architecture diagram showing who owns keys (vendor vs. customer-managed).
- Access control: list of admin accounts, SSO/IdP config, MFA enforcement policy.
- Change management: recent change log snippets for the last 6 months (PRs, release notes) + incident postmortems for any security incidents in the period.
- Subprocessor list + mappings to their attestations (we need evidence that critical subprocessors have SOC2/ISO or equivalent).
- Data flows: short diagram + CSV of where Redwood PII/PHI (if any) lands in vendor systems.
- Retention & deletion: policy excerpt and an example deletion confirmation for a sample record.
- Pen testing: latest external penetration test report and remediation tracker.

Key questions to raise (unique angles):
- For vendors using customer-managed KMS: can we get audit logging of key operations (encrypt/decrypt) for a 30-day window? Is that exportable?
- If vendor is multi-tenant on same cluster: can they show logical isolation proof (namespace/pod mapping) for our tenant?
- Are there any subcontractors that process tokens/session data transiently (e.g., caching layers) that don't appear on the contract?
- Bridge letters: will the vendor sign a scoped bridge letter that covers the specific services we use (not just an org-level blanket)?
- Evidence freshness: what is their cadence for producing evidence (monthly/quarterly) and how much lead time do they need?

Logistics / transfer options (pros/cons):
- Shared S3 bucket (encrypted, restricted put by vendor role): easy, automatable, but needs cross-account IAM and TTL enforcement.
- Encrypted email (PGP) with signed manifest: low tech, but brittle for large artifacts and auditor workflows.
- Secure Share (Box/OneDrive) with expiring links and audit logging: familiar to vendors, supports granular access control.
- Direct upload into our evidence tracking repo (constrained by vendor onboarding permissions).
Recommendation: prefer cross-account S3 with object-lock disabled, object lifecycle 180 days, and a write-only role for vendor with PutObject only. Auditors granted read-only role for that bucket for the audit window.

Naming & metadata convention (we should lock this down now):
- <vendor>-<control-id>-<artifact-type>-<YYYYMMDD>.<ext>
- Metadata fields to require on upload: uploader_name, uploader_email, control_id, evidence_description, service_scope.
- Example: alpha-engineering-CC6-change-log-20250109.csv

Negotiation levers / redlines to prepare:
- Right to audit: scoping language to limit to controls that impact Redwood processing.
- Bridge letters: require explicit service mapping and timeframe.
- Subprocessor disclosure: require 30-day notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor that may process customer data.
- Remediation SLA: vendor commits to 45 days for medium/high security defects or a documented remediation plan with milestones.

Potential blockers & notes to raise:
- Some vendors insist on not sharing full SOC reports (redact org-level info). Need to clarify if redactions are acceptable to our auditor.
- Legacy vendors that rotate keys but can't provide rotation logs — may need compensating controls (e.g., snapshot of KMS policy + attestation letter).
- Timezone constraints: vendors EMEA/APAC may have 5–7 business day lead time for artifact pulls.

Action items (assign now in the 1:1):
- Sloane: finalize evidence matrix template + drop into Confluence (due 2025-02-06).
- Ibrahim: validate vendor inventory + flag any missing contracts (due 2025-02-04).
- Noelle: draft IAM role and bucket policy for cross-account S3 evidence transfer (due 2025-02-07).
- Vendor Assurance lead: confirm which vendors can provide SOC2/bridge letter by 2025-02-10.
- Assign control owners in product/infra for top 5 vendor controls (due 2025-02-12).

Notes to self / talking style:
- Be pragmatic: vendors that are small/startups might not have perfect artifacts; aim for compensating controls and timeline rather than hard rejections.
- Don't accept vague timelines — get dates (not 'ASAP').
- If they push back on RTA, ask for their standard SOC2/ISO attestation and an escalation path to legal for an exception.

Open questions I need answered before vendor call:
- Do auditors accept redacted SOC2 reports for subprocessors? (ask audit lead)
- Is 180-day TTL on evidence bucket sufficient for external auditors or do they need full retention for 3 years?
- Can we get an internal legal sign-off on the RTA scoping language I propose?

Quick reference links (internal):
- Vendor risk playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/VENDOR-PLAYBOOK
- Evidence naming pattern doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EVIDENCE-NAMES

End of memo — want this short and actionable for the 1:1. If the Vendor Assurance lead wants a pre-send to the vendor, we should include the evidence matrix as a one-page PDF.
